relevance_reason: Reports a novel SHOC2 RASopathy-causing variant with prenatal-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and functional studies; SHOC2 mutation causes Mazzanti syndrome (NSLH1).

findings.statement: Motta et al. (2019) reported a third RASopathy-causing SHOC2 mutation, c.807_808delinsTT (p.Gln269_His270delinsHisTyr), which was associated with prenatal-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
quotes: Here, we report on the third RASopathy-causing SHOC2 mutation (c.807_808delinsTT, p.Gln269_His270delinsHisTyr), which was found associated with prenatal-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

findings.statement: Structural analyses by Motta et al. (2019) indicated that the SHOC2 Q269_H270delinsHY mutation might affect the relative orientation of the two leucine-rich repeat domains. Functional studies showed enhanced binding of the mutant protein to MRAS and PPP1CB and increased signaling through the MAPK cascade, supporting an activating role; unlike SHOC2 S2G, the mutant was not constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane.
quotes: Structural analyses indicated a possible impact of the mutation on the relative orientation of the two SHOC2's leucine-rich repeat domains.
Functional studies provided evidence of its activating role, revealing enhanced binding of the mutant protein to MRAS and PPP1CB, and increased signaling through the MAPK cascade.
Differing from SHOC2 S2G , SHOC2 Q269_H270delinsHY is not constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane.

findings.statement: Motta et al. (2019) concluded that diverse mechanisms of SHOC2 functional dysregulation converge toward upregulation of MAPK signaling.
quotes: These data document that diverse mechanisms in SHOC2 functional dysregulation converge toward MAPK signaling upregulation.

relevance_reason: Functional study showing that Noonan syndrome mutations in SHOC2 (the NSLH1 gene), MRAS and PPP1CB enhance SHOC2-MRAS-PP1 complex formation, giving a mechanism for disease

findings.statement: Young et al. (2018) showed that MRAS interacts with SHOC2 and protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to form a heterotrimeric holoenzyme that dephosphorylates the inhibitory S259 site on RAF kinases (S259 on CRAF, S365 on BRAF). MRAS and SHOC2 acted as PP1 regulatory subunits that make the complex highly specific for RAF. MRAS also acted as a targeting subunit, because the complex needed membrane localization to dephosphorylate RAF efficiently and to regulate the ERK pathway in cells.
quotes: The MRAS GTPase, a close relative of RAS oncoproteins, interacts with SHOC2 and protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to form a heterotrimeric holoenzyme that dephosphorylates this S259 RAF site.
MRAS and SHOC2 function as PP1 regulatory subunits providing the complex with striking specificity against RAF.
MRAS also functions as a targeting subunit as membrane localization is required for efficient RAF dephosphorylation and ERK pathway regulation in cells.

findings.statement: Young et al. (2018) showed that Noonan syndrome mutations in SHOC2, MRAS and PPP1CB always promoted formation of the complex with the other two partners, but did not necessarily promote binding to other interactors. The authors concluded that Noonan syndrome in people with SHOC2, MRAS or PPP1CB mutations is likely driven at the biochemical level by enhanced ternary complex formation.
quotes: MRAS, SHOC2, and PPP1CB are mutated in Noonan syndrome, and we show that syndromic mutations invariably promote complex formation with each other, but not necessarily with other interactors.
Thus, Noonan syndrome in individuals with SHOC2, MRAS, or PPPC1B mutations is likely driven at the biochemical level by enhanced ternary complex formation

findings.statement: Young et al. (2018) reported that the predicted structure of SHOC2 closely resembles the A subunit of PP2A, which they suggested was a case of convergent structural evolution. They identified several regions in SHOC2 involved in complex formation, as well as residues in MRAS switch I and the interswitch region that help explain why MRAS binds specifically to SHOC2-PP1.
quotes: SHOC2's predicted structure shows remarkable similarities to the A subunit of PP2A, suggesting a case of convergent structural evolution with the PP2A heterotrimer.

We have identified multiple regions in SHOC2 involved in complex formation as well as residues in MRAS switch I and the interswitch region that help account for MRAS's unique effector specificity for SHOC2-PP1.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with a PPP1CB mutation (a related Noonan-like disorder with loose anagen hair), not the SHOC2-related NSLH1. It gives context on phenotypic overlap and genetic heterogeneity only.

findings.statement: Bertola et al. (2017) reported a 12-year-old Brazilian boy with the recurrent p.Pro49Arg mutation in PPP1CB, a gene newly associated with RASopathies. He had sparse, thin, slow-growing hair resembling the ectodermal finding typical of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair, and also had craniosynostosis. The authors concluded that PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair shares great similarity with Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair.
quotes: We report on a 12-year-old Brazilian boy with the p.Pro49Arg mutation in PPP1CB, a novel gene associated with RASopathies.
he also showed the same hair pattern-sparse, thin, and with slow growing-, similar to the typical ectodermal finding observed in Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair
This report gives further support that this novel RASopathy-PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair-shares great similarity to Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair

relevance_reason: Reports a second SHOC2 variant (M173I) in a father and daughter with a mild RASopathy phenotype that partly overlaps NS/LAH, with functional studies. This expands the SHOC2-related phenotype spectrum.

findings.statement: Hannig et al. (2014) reported a 5-year-old girl of European ancestry, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who had right optic nerve hypoplasia, bilateral nystagmus, speech delay, poor hair growth, and hyperactive behavior. She had average stature, macrocephaly (98th percentile), sparse and slow-growing hair that was not loose, normal skin pigmentation, bilateral ptosis, widely spaced nipples, and clubbed nails. MRI showed multiple irregularities of unknown significance in the midbrain, pons, and medulla. She did not have short stature, a cardiac anomaly, hyperpigmentation, ichthyosis, or loose anagen hair.
quotes: The first patient is a 5 year old female referred for evaluation of right optic nerve hypoplasia, bilateral nystagmus, speech delay, poor hair growth and hyperactive behavior.

She had average stature (47th percentile), macrocephaly (98th percentile), sparse and slow-growing hair which was not loose, normal skin pigmentation, bilateral ptosis and nystagmus, normal chest with wide-spaced nipples, and clubbed nails
She does not have short stature, a cardiac anomaly, hyperpigmentation, ichthyosis or loose anagen hair.

findings.statement: Hannig et al. (2014) found that the proband's father, who carried the same SHOC2 variant, was tall (6 feet 3 inches) and had intellectual disability, a high-arched palate, sparse hair, and clubbed nails. His features were very subtle and did not clearly indicate a RASopathy apart from the sparse hair and clubbed nails. Echocardiograms and renal ultrasounds were negative in both the father and the proband.
quotes: He was 6′3″ tall, had intellectual disability, a high-arched palate, sparse hair and clubbed nails
Her father has tall stature and very subtle clinical features that do not clearly denote a Rasopathy, other than his sparse hair and clubbed nails.
Echocardiograms and renal ultrasounds on both patients were negative

findings.statement: In the girl and her father, Hannig et al. (2014) found a heterozygous variant in the SHOC2 gene, c.519G>A (p.M173I), by sequencing a RASopathy gene panel. The proband inherited the variant from her father. It was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals. Met173 is located in leucine-rich repeat 4 and is conserved among vertebrate SHOC2 orthologs.
quotes: DNA sequencing of a Rasopathy gene panel including BRAF, CBL, HRAS, KRAS, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, NRAS, PTPN11, RAF1 SHOC2 and SOS1 identified a novel heterozygous SHOC2 variant c.519G>A; p.M173I.
This variant was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals. Both parents were tested, and our proband’s father had a heterozygous copy of the p.M173I variant.
The Met173 amino acid residue of SHOC2 is located in the fourth leucine-rich repeat (LRR4) of the SHOC2 LRR domain and is conserved among all SHOC2 vertebrate orthologues

findings.statement: Hannig et al. (2014) found that in SHOC2-depleted Cos1 cells, the M173I mutant restored EGF-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation by only about 10% above basal levels, whereas wildtype SHOC2 fully rescued it. The mutant's half-life, subcellular localization, and binding to M-RAS and RAF1 were unchanged. However, it failed to precipitate PP1c effectively and produced only a mild increase in RAF1 Ser338 phosphorylation. The authors concluded that p.M173I causes loss of function in the ERK1/2 pathway.
quotes: the SHOC2 (M173I)-tRFP mutant expressed to a similar level as WT SHOC2-tRFP was only able to restore ~10% above the basal level of EGF-induced ERK1/2 activity
the GST-tagged M173I mutant of SHOC2 failed to precipitate endogenous PP1c effectively, suggesting that the M173I substitution alters the interaction of SHOC2 and PP1c.
The p.M173I SHOC2 substitution causes loss of function in the ERK1/2 pathway.

findings.statement: Hannig et al. (2014) noted that patients with the M173I variant differed markedly from NS/LAH patients with the S2G mutation. The proband had NS-like craniofacial features and CFC-like sparse hair but did not have short stature, cardiac defects, or loose anagen hair. The authors concluded that SHOC2 mutations can cause a spectrum of RASopathy phenotypes of varying severity.
quotes: Phenotypic features of patients with the M173I mutation are significantly different from those reported for patients with the c.4A>G; p.S2G SHOC2 mutation.
We thus conclude that SHOC2 mutations can cause a spectrum of Rasopathy phenotypes of varying severity.

relevance_reason: The paper reports 5 patients with the SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly mutation that causes Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair. It adds new features: structural brain anomalies and myelofibrosis.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) reported 5 male patients with Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair carrying the SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly mutation. All 5 had skin hyperpigmentation, sparse light-colored hair, increased fine wrinkles, ligamentous laxity and developmental delay. All 4 who were assessed had a structural cardiac anomaly. Hypotonia and macrocephaly were each present in 4 of 5. Polyhydramnios, increased birth weight and feeding tube use were each present in 3 of 5. All had unusually long eyelashes (dolichocilia).
quotes: We report five patients with this mutation. All had skin hyperpigmentation, sparse light colored hair, increased fine wrinkles, ligamentous laxity, developmental delay, and 4/4 had a structural cardiac anomaly.
Hypotonia and macrocephaly occurred in 4/5 (80%); 3/5 (60%) had polyhydramnios, increased birth weight or required use of a feeding tube.
In contrast to the slow growing scalp hair, all had unusually long eye lashes, but none requiring trimming of the lashes.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) described distinctive brain abnormalities in patients with SHOC2 mutations. These were relative megalencephaly with enlarged subarachnoid spaces suggestive of benign external hydrocephalus, and a relatively small posterior fossa indicated by a vertical tentorium (4 of 4). The authors suggested that this combination accounted for the high rate of cerebellar tonsillar ectopia (3 of 4). Including literature cases, 3 of 8 patients who had MRI showed a Chiari I malformation.
quotes: Distinctive brain abnormalities included relative megalencephaly and enlarged subarachnoid spaces suggestive of benign external hydrocephalus, and a relatively small posterior fossa as indicated by a vertical tentorium.
The combination of a large brain with a small posterior fossa likely resulted in the high rate of cerebellar tonsillar ectopia (3/4; 75%).
Adding the patient in whom a MRI obtained at age 9 years revealed a Chiari 1 malformation, 3/8 patients in whom MRIs were obtained had a Chiari 1.

phenotypes.text: small posterior fossa with vertical tentorium

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) described patient 1, a boy born to 37-year-old parents after a pregnancy complicated by polyhydramnios and cystic hygroma. He was macrosomic at birth and had pyloric stenosis, severe failure to thrive needing a gastrostomy tube, mild pulmonic valve stenosis, low axial tone, small optic nerves, motor delay, and an OFC of +3 SD. At age 2 years 3 months, juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia was suspected. He developed hepatosplenomegaly, and bone marrow biopsy was most consistent with primary myelofibrosis, with a normal karyotype, no monosomy 7 and no JAK2 p.Val617Phe mutation. He died at age 2.5 years after splenectomy done in preparation for bone marrow transplant. This was the first hematologic neoplasm reported with a SHOC2 mutation.
quotes: Bone marrow biopsies revealed markedly hypercellular marrow with crush artifacts suggestive of fibrosis and marked generalized increase in reticulin staining consistent with myelofibrosis.

Allele specific PCR assay for the JAK2 p.Val617Phe mutation associated with non-CML myeloproliferative disorders on bone marrow derived DNA was negative. All bone marrow study results were most consistent with primary myelofibrosis.
He died at age 2 ½ years after splenectomy in preparation for a bone marrow transplant.

findings.statement: In 5 patients with Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair, Gripp et al. (2013) identified the recurrent SHOC2 c.4A>G mutation (p.Ser2Gly). In patient 1, it was found by postmortem testing of buccal DNA and was absent from both parents. The mutation was also de novo in patient 2. Sequencing of other RASopathy genes was normal in the patients.
quotes: Postmortem testing of stored buccal cell derived DNA performed on a research basis revealed the recurrent SHOC2 c.4A>G mutation. This change was not present in either parent’s buccal cell derived DNA.
SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly | +, de novo | +, de novo | + | + | +

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) described patient 4, a boy of Mexican ancestry with global developmental delay and mild to moderate intellectual disability. He had an ASD, blond, sparse, easily pluckable hair, and long eyelashes. Brain MRI showed mild ventriculomegaly, periventricular nodular heterotopia, and a thick, dysplastic corpus callosum. By age 6 years he had developed a Chiari I malformation with platybasia and basilar invagination, along with C3–C4 vertebral fusion and unusual venous sinus anatomy. Periventricular nodular heterotopia had not previously been reported with a SHOC2 mutation.
quotes: A brain MRI revealed mild ventriculomegaly and subependymal heterotopia (Fig. 2). Subsequent brain and spinal MRIs performed at 6 years due to headaches revealed development of a Chiari 1 malformation (Table II) in the context of platybasia and basilar invagination, and segmental fusion of the C3 and C4 vertebrae.
Periventricular nodular heterotopia was seen in one patient with a thick and dysplastic corpus callosum.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) described patient 3, a boy with biventricular hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and right bundle branch block at age 6 months, later aortic insufficiency and mild pulmonic stenosis, and an OFC of +5 SD at age 9 years. He had severe aggressive behavior and was diagnosed with pervasive developmental disorder and Tourette syndrome, for which he took psychotropic medication.
quotes: He had right bundle branch block, and mild to moderate biventricular hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) at age 6 months.
He was diagnosed with pervasive developmental disorder and Tourette syndrome at 9 years and continued to use psychotropic medications.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) noted that patient 1 lacked the common somatic JAK2 mutation, which is present in most patients with myelofibrosis. They suggested that germline or somatic SHOC2 mutation, through activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway, may be causally involved in myelofibrosis.
quotes: The absence of a somatic JAK2 mutation, seen in the majority of patients with myelofibrosis, is noteworthy as it suggests that germline or somatic SHOC2 mutations are causally involved in myelofibrosis.
In the absence of the common somatic JAK2 mutation this suggests activation of the Ras/MAPK pathway as an alternative initiating step towards myeloproliferative disorders.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) noted that 4 of their 5 patients had originally been suspected of having Costello syndrome. They subjectively observed that the ectodermal, growth and developmental features of SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly patients closely resembled those of Costello syndrome due to HRAS p.Gly13Cys, and they supported a gene panel approach to molecular testing.
quotes: It is noteworthy that Patients 1, 2, 3 and 5 in our series were suspected of having Costello syndrome, a rasopathy sharing phenotypic findings with Noonan syndrome.
Subjectively, individuals with HRAS p.Gly13Cys and SHOC2 p.Gly2Ser closely resemble each other in their ectodermal, growth and developmental findings.

findings.statement: Gripp et al. (2013) combined earlier case series (12 of 188 mutation-negative Noonan or Noonan-like patients) to estimate that SHOC2 mutations account for about 6% of mutation-negative Noonan syndrome. This corresponds to about 1.8% of all individuals with Noonan syndrome.
quotes: Assuming no overlap between these case series, the incidence of a SHOC2 mutation is 12/188, or about 6%. However, at least 70% of all Noonan syndrome patients have a mutation in a previously reported gene; thus 6% of the remaining 30% would reflect 1.8% of all individuals with Noonan syndrome.

relevance_reason: Case report of an infant with the recurrent de novo SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly mutation (cause of NSLH1) presenting with fetal distress and fatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which the authors say expands the phenotype.

findings.statement: Hoban et al. (2012) reported a male infant with Noonan syndrome due to a SHOC2 mutation. He was delivered prematurely at 32 weeks because of fetal distress. After birth he had dysmorphic features, edema, hepatosplenomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and respiratory distress. An echocardiogram showed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. The cardiac lesion progressed quickly, and he was discharged home for palliative care. The authors stated that his cardiac findings and features were not typical of individuals previously reported with this mutation and thus expanded the clinical phenotype.
quotes: The male infant presented with fetal distress requiring premature delivery at 32 weeks and was noted to have dysmorphic features, edema, hepatosplenomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and respiratory distress following birth.
An echocardiogram revealed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. The infant's cardiac lesion rapidly progressed, and he was discharged home for palliative care.
The patient's cardiac findings and features were not typical for those individuals previously reported with this SHOC2 mutation and thus expand the clinical phenotype.

findings.statement: In this infant with Noonan syndrome and fatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Hoban et al. (2012) identified a de novo missense mutation in SHOC2 predicting p.Ser2Gly. It was found by clinical testing of genes that cause Noonan syndrome and related disorders. The authors noted that this pathogenic mutation had been reported before.
quotes: Clinical testing of genes causative of Noonan syndrome and related disorders detected the previously reported, pathogenic, de novo SHOC2 missense mutation predicting p.Ser2Gly.

relevance_reason: Reports SHOC2 p.S2G mutation in 8 patients with Noonan-like syndrome and characterizes their phenotype, including loose anagen hair.

findings.statement: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) analyzed SHOC2 in 92 patients with Noonan syndrome and related disorders who did not have mutations in PTPN11, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, MAP2K1/2, SOS1, or RAF1, and found the previously identified p.S2G mutation in 8 patients.
quotes: we analyzed SHOC2 in 92 patients with Noonan syndrome and related disorders who did not exhibit PTPN11, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, MAP2K1/2, SOS1 or RAF1 mutations. We found the previously identified p.S2G mutation in eight of our patients.

findings.statement: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) reported that all 8 patients with the SHOC2 p.S2G mutation had short stature, sparse hair, and atopic skin; 6 had severe mental retardation and easily pluckable hair, and 1 had leukocytosis. The authors concluded that easily pluckable/loose anagen hair is distinctive in SHOC2 mutation-positive patients, whose features partially overlap with typical Noonan or CFC syndrome.
quotes: All the patients with the p.S2G mutation showed short stature, sparse hair and atopic skin. Six of the mutation-positive patients showed severe mental retardation and easily pluckable hair, and one showed leukocytosis.
show that easily pluckable/loose anagen hair is distinctive in SHOC2 mutation-positive patients

findings.statement: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) developed a rapid melting curve analysis-based detection system for the SHOC2 p.S2G mutation for screening of this apparently common mutation.
quotes: We developed a rapid detection system to identify the p.S2G mutation using melting curve analysis, which will be a useful tool to screen for the apparently common mutation.

findings.statement: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) identified no SHOC2 mutations in leukemia cells from 82 leukemia patients.
quotes: No SHOC2 mutations were identified in leukemia cells from 82 leukemia patients.

relevance_reason: Identifies the SHOC2 S2G de novo mutation as the cause of Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair, with clinical characterization and functional studies.

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) used an in silico protein network analysis seeded with known RAS/MAPK mutant proteins to prioritize SHOC2 as a candidate Noonan syndrome gene. Sequencing of SHOC2 in 96 Noonan syndrome patients negative for mutations in known genes identified a heterozygous 4A-G transition predicting a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution in 4 unrelated sporadic individuals; the mutation was absent from the parents in the 3 families tested (paternity confirmed), indicating de novo origin, and was present in several tissues, indicating germline transmission.
quotes: Resequencing of coding exons for the best candidate, SHOC2, in a NS cohort including 96 individuals who were negative for mutations in known disease genes
revealed an A-to-G transition at position 4 of the gene, predicting the Ser2Gly amino acid substitution (S2G), in four unrelated individuals
All cases were sporadic, and genotyping of parental DNAs available for three of the four subjects documented the absence of the sequence variant in the parents and confirmed paternity in each family

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) analyzed SHOC2 in a further 410 mutation-negative subjects with Noonan syndrome or a related phenotype and found the 4A>G (S2G) change in 21, with de novo occurrence proven in the 12 families with available parental DNA. No other disease-associated SHOC2 variant was found, suggesting a specific pathogenetic role for S2G; in total 25 subjects shared the mutation.
quotes: We then analyzed SHOC2 in a cohort of 410 mutation-negative subjects with NS or a related phenotype. We observed 21 with the 4A>G missense change and proved that mutations were de novo in twelve families from which parental DNAs were available.
No additional disease-associated SHOC2 sequence variant was identified in the analyzed cohort, strongly suggesting a specific pathogenetic role for the S2G amino acid substitution.

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) found that SHOC2 S2G mutation-positive individuals shared a consistent phenotype previously termed Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair: Noonan-like facies (macrocephaly, high forehead, hypertelorism, ptosis, low-set posteriorly rotated ears, short webbed neck, pectus anomalies), reduced growth frequently with proven GH deficiency, cognitive deficits, hyperactive behavior that improved with age, and easily pluckable, sparse, thin, slow-growing hair, with loose anagen hair confirmed microscopically in 12. Most had darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis, cardiac anomalies were common with mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects overrepresented, and the voice was hypernasal. Several were thought to resemble Costello or cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome in infancy.
quotes: they exhibited reduced growth, which was frequently associated with proven GH deficiency, cognitive deficits, distinctive hyperactive behaviour that improved with age in most subjects, and hair anomalies including easily pluckable, sparse, thin, slow growing hair
In twelve subjects, a diagnosis of loose anagen hair was confirmed by microscopic examination of pulled hairs. Most of them also exhibited darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.

Cardiac anomalies were observed in the majority of the cases, with dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects significantly overrepresented compared with the general NS population. The voice was characteristically hypernasal.

phenotypes.text: easily pluckable sparse thin slow-growing hair

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that the S2G substitution creates an N-myristoylation site: SHOC2 S2G expressed in Cos-1 cells incorporated [3H]-myristic acid, whereas wildtype SHOC2 and a disease-unrelated S2A mutant did not.
quotes: SHOC2S2G incorporated [3H]-myristic acid, while the wild type protein and the disease-unrelated SHOC2S2A did not.
in silico analysis predicted myristoylation of the SHOC2S2G mutant with high confidence

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) found that wildtype SHOC2 was distributed in cytoplasm and nucleus in starved Cos-1 cells and translocated to the nucleus upon EGF stimulation (also seen for endogenous SHOC2 in primary fibroblasts), whereas SHOC2 S2G was constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane, dependent on myristoylation (reversed by an NMT inhibitor), and failed to translocate to the nucleus. The mutant did not heterodimerize with wildtype, excluding a dominant-negative effect, and it enhanced EGF-dependent ERK phosphorylation in Neuro2A cells but not in Cos-1 or 293T cells, indicating cell type-specific MAPK activation.
quotes: SHOC2wt was uniformly distributed in the cytoplasm and nucleus in starved cells but was restricted to the nucleus following EGF stimulation
In contrast, SHOC2S2G was specifically targeted to the cell membrane in both states.
SHOC2S2G expression promoted enhanced EGF-dependent ERK phosphorylation compared to wild type SHOC2, in neuroblastoma Neuro2A cells

findings.statement: Cordeddu et al. (2009) found in C. elegans that wildtype human SHOC2, but not S2G, could functionally replace SUR-8 in a sur-8rf;let-60gof background, and S2G did not act as a dominant negative. Expression of SHOC2 S2G or myristoylation-tagged wildtype SHOC2 at early L3 caused protruding vulva, egg-laying defects and bag-of-worms phenotypes due to abnormal vulval morphogenesis (asymmetric invaginations involving P5.p/P7.p descendants in 17/48 S2G larvae), without altered vulval cell fate specification; these proteins were membrane-targeted in worm cells.
quotes: While SHOC2wt was able to replace SUR-8 functionally, SHOC2S2G failed to do so.

at early L3 stage, it caused abnormal vulval development, resulting in protruding vulva (Pvl), decreased egg laying efficiency (Egl) and accumulation of larvae inside the mother with the formation of bag-of-worms adults (Bag phenotype)
in larvae expressing SHOC2S2G (17/48) or myr::SHOC2wt (10/22), descendants of VPCs P5.p and/or P7.p also detached from the cuticle, resulting in larger and asymmetric invaginations

relevance_reason: The original clinical description of three children that led to the proposed new syndrome, Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair (Mazzanti syndrome).

findings.statement: Mazzanti et al. (2003) described 3 children with short stature, the same facial phenotype, macrocephaly, enlarged cerebrospinal fluid spaces, short neck with redundant skin, severe growth hormone deficiency, and mild psychomotor delay with attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Two of the children had mild dilatation of the pulmonary root. All 3 had a unique combination of ectodermal abnormalities, including darkly pigmented hairless skin and hair defined as loose anagen hair.
quotes: We present three children with short stature, the same facial phenotype, macrocephaly, enlarged cerebral spinal fluid spaces, short neck with redundant skin, severe GH deficiency, mild psychomotor delay with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), mild dilatation of the pulmonary root in two of them, and a unique combination of ectodermal abnormalities.
darkly pigmented and hairless skin, and the unusual aspect of the hair, defined as loose anagen hair syndrome

phenotypes.text: mild dilatation of the pulmonary root

findings.statement: Mazzanti et al. (2003) concluded that the children's appearance, which was not completely typical of Noonan syndrome, together with the behavioral phenotype, GH deficiency, darkly pigmented hairless skin, and loose anagen hair, did not fit any known condition. They postulated that the children might represent a distinct, previously unreported syndrome, which they proposed to name 'Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.'
quotes: Their appearance, not completely typical of Noonan syndrome, the behavioral phenotype, GH deficiency, darkly pigmented and hairless skin, and the unusual aspect of the hair, defined as loose anagen hair syndrome did not fit any known condition.
We postulate that these children may represent a distinct, previously unreported syndrome that we would name "Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair".

relevance_reason: Case series of loose anagen hair that includes a 5-year-old boy with Noonan syndrome and loose anagen hair, which is the defining combination of this entry; other patients have isolated LAH.

findings.statement: Tosti et al. (1997) reported 19 patients diagnosed with loose anagen hair (LAH) at a university medical center beginning in 1990: 14 children and 5 adults, aged 8 months to 47 years. Associated diseases included Noonan syndrome in a 5-year-old boy and alopecia areata in a 3-year-old boy. In all cases a trichogram showed mostly anagen hairs (80 to 100%) without sheaths.
quotes: Beginning in January 1990, 14 children and 5 adults (age range, 8 months to 47 years) were diagnosed as having LAH. Associated diseases included alopecia areata in a 3-year-old boy and Noonan syndrome in a 5-year-old boy.
In all cases, findings of a trichogram showed a predominance of anagen hairs (80% to 100%) devoid of sheaths.

findings.statement: Among the patients with LAH reported by Tosti et al. (1997), 2 adults were parents of 2 affected children. The other 3 adults were the only members of their families with LAH. The authors concluded that LAH may be sporadic, may occur together with developmental or acquired conditions, or, less commonly, may be familial.
quotes: Two adult patients were parents of 2 affected children; the other 3 adults were the only members of their families with LAH.
The development of LAH may be sporadic, occur in association with developmental or acquired conditions, or, less commonly, be a familial disorder.

findings.statement: Tosti et al. (1997) found that LAH can begin in adulthood: 3 sporadic adults had diffuse hair shedding that started suddenly 1 to 3 years before evaluation. They noted that adult-onset LAH can easily be misdiagnosed as telogen hair loss. On follow-up, LAH stayed stable in 4 children and 1 adult, and hair density improved considerably in 2 children and 1 adult.
quotes: These 3 patients presented with a diffuse hair shedding that had suddenly developed 1 to 3 years before our observation.
In 4 children and 1 adult the condition remained stable; in 2 children and 1 adult, a considerable improvement in hair density was noticed.
While adult-onset LAH may not be exceptional, it can be easily misdiagnosed as telogen hair loss.

findings.statement: Tosti et al. (1997) studied the pathology of hair from 5 patients. Apart from frequent fragmentation of the inner root sheath, they found no morphologic abnormalities of the hair follicles. They concluded that pathologic findings are of little diagnostic value in LAH.
quotes: The pathologic study of hair from 5 patients did not reveal morphological abnormalities of the hair follicles except for a high incidence of fragmentations of the inner root sheath.
The pathologic findings of LAH do not demonstrate any specific features and are of little value in the diagnosis of this condition.

relevance_reason: This is the original case report of Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair, the disorder this entry describes (alternative title Tosti syndrome).

findings.statement: Tosti et al. (1991) reported a 4.5-year-old girl with Noonan syndrome and loose anagen hair. Her hair was short and blond, had never been cut, and was easily plucked. Trichogram showed that nearly all bulbs were abnormally shaped anagen bulbs lacking inner and outer root sheaths. Scalp biopsy showed marked cleft formation between fragmented inner root sheaths and irregularly shaped hair shafts.
quotes: We report on a 4 1/2-year-old girl affected by loose anagen hair and Noonan's syndrome. The girl had short, blond, easily pluckable hair that had never been cut.
The trichogram showed an absolute prevalence of abnormally shaped anagen bulbs lacking inner and outer root sheaths.
A scalp biopsy evidenced a marked cleft formation between fragmented inner root sheaths and irregularly shaped hair shafts.

phenotypes.text: short hair that had never been cut
abnormally shaped anagen bulbs lacking root sheaths
cleft formation between fragmented inner root sheaths and irregular hair shafts on scalp biopsy
